subject: Token throttle impact: throughput shortfall and contract workback
messages:
From: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@altmetrics.io>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Turner <mike.turner@altmetrics.io>, AltMetrics Legal <legal@altmetrics.io>
Date: 2027-11-28T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — tokens throttled and job failures

Rishi,

We experienced a significant throughput regression across our batch scoring jobs starting late on 11/26 and continuing through this morning. Symptoms we saw:
- Token-level throttling from your API that caused retry storms in our workers (error rate spiked from ~0.6% to ~6.2%).
- Median token latency increased ~4.5x for our 2–4k token requests.
- Overall throughput to our committed concurrency dipped ~18% during peak windows, causing missed SLAs on customer-facing reports.

We attached error logs and sample request IDs. This incident directly impacted our November reporting window and increased our operational costs due to retries. We need:
1) A clear timeline and root cause analysis.
2) A proposed credit or refund for the impacted period and concrete remediation commitments.
3) An executive-level point of contact; our COO Mike Turner will be monitoring.

Please respond with an interim mitigation plan and your expected cadence for a post-incident report.

Thanks,
Erin Zhao
Head of Data Platform
AltMetrics

Attachments: error_logs_2027-11-26_to_1128.csv
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@altmetrics.io>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — tokens throttled and job failures

Hi Erin —

First, I’m sorry for the disruption. We’ve prioritized your traffic and engaged infra to mitigate the token-contend issue. Immediate actions already taken:
- Redirected AltMetrics traffic to a quieter GPU pool and lifted a conservative concurrency cap that inadvertently interacted poorly with your request mix.
- Enabled a short-term KV cache warmup to reduce duplicate prefix work for your long-context requests.
- Ops has flagged all '429'-type errors and is tracing root cause (INF-9182).

We will:
1) Provide an incident timeline and RCA draft by EOD Friday (Nov 3).
2) Share a provisional credit calculation within 24 hours — initial estimate will be a provisional invoice credit to cover demonstrable throughput shortfall while we complete the final SLO measurement.
3) Schedule a 30-minute exec review with you and our leadership to align on remediation and contract steps.

As an immediate remediation, we can bump your burst capacity for two weeks at no additional charge so your November reporting jobs can rerun without throttling. If you want that enabled now, say the word and I’ll get ops to apply it.

I’ve attached the logs you sent into our ticket for tracking.

On Mon, Nov 28, 2027 at 09:17, Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@altmetrics.io> wrote:
> Rishi,
> 
> We experienced a significant throughput regression...

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Director — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: error_logs_2027-11-26_to_1128.csv (as received)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: AltMetrics token-throttle — provisional compensation calc

Team —

Summary: AltMetrics saw ~18% below committed throughput across their Nov 26–28 high-volume window. Error-rate and retry amplification materially increased egress costs on their side; they're asking for credits and a formal contract workback.

Attachments: altmetrics_slo_delta_1126-1128.xlsx (breakdown)

Quick numbers (provisional):
- Committed monthly spend: $350,000 (contracted).
- Observed impacted window: 72 hours (11/26 22:00 UTC — 11/28 22:00 UTC).
- Estimated lost-served-tokens equivalent: 18% of expected in-window throughput (~$12.5k worth of billable units).

Proposed provisional concession (to close immediate exec concern and avoid churn):
- Issue a provisional invoice credit of $17,500 (~5% of monthly commitment) applied to next invoice. Rationale: covers demonstrable shortfall + goodwill for retry costs; final credit to be reconciled after RCA and precise SLO calculation.
- Offer two-week burst-cap uplift (already proposed to customer).
- Ticket INF-9182 to track RCA and kernel patch work; target patch rollout by 2027-12-07.

Risks: legal will want a clean audit trail and a contract amendment if we convert provisional credit into formal remediation. Finance needs an approved memo for the credit.

Next actions: Ben to draft the provisional credit memo for Finance/Legal; Lauren to prepare the SOW/timeline for the kernel/ops changes; I’ll coordinate the exec call with AltMetrics (propose Wed 11/30 14:00 PST).

Rishi

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@altmetrics.io>
Date: 2027-11-30T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Token throttle impact: throughput shortfall and contract workback

Erin —

Thanks for flagging and for working with Rishi while we triage. Reducing customer toil is our priority. To be clear on Redwood's commitment while we finish the RCA:

1) Provisional credit: Redwood will issue a provisional invoice credit of $17,500 to AltMetrics, applied to the next monthly invoice. This is provisional pending final SLO reconciliation and a completed RCA. If final calculations materially differ, we will reconcile once the RCA is complete.

2) Remediation commitments: Ops/Infra will push the targeted kernel patch (see INF-9182) to your quieter pool by 2027-12-07. We will also extend a two-week burst uplift at no cost to ensure your November jobs complete cleanly.

3) Governance: Legal and Finance will prepare a short amendment that documents the provisional credit and the reconciliation process. Ben — please raise the memo for approval today. Lauren — please draft an SOW and a timeline for the patch and the enablement steps for AltMetrics.

4) Executive touchpoint: I’ll join the Wed 11/30 14:00 PST call to review the RCA outline and next steps.

We want to resolve this quickly and transparently. If AltMetrics prefers a different cadence or a larger immediate concession to accelerate, let us know — we’ll escalate accordingly.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@altmetrics.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Erin Zhao <erin.zhao@altmetrics.io>, AltMetrics Legal <legal@altmetrics.io>
Date: 2027-11-30T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Token throttle impact: throughput shortfall and contract workback

Vivek, Rishi, Ben —

Thank you for the quick attention and for the provisional credit offer. AltMetrics is willing to accept the provisional $17,500 credit subject to:
- Receipt of the credit memo and a short amendment documenting the reconciliation process (legal review required).
- A firm SOW and milestone dates for the kernel patch and for the two-week burst uplift.
- DocuSign-ready amendment preferred; please include an acceptance deadline so our finance/legal teams can close this quickly.

We appreciate the two-week uplift while you complete the RCA — that will allow us to get November jobs back on cycle. We’ll join the exec call at 14:00 PST to align.

Mike Turner
COO, AltMetrics

Attachments referenced in thread: provisional_credit_calc_1128.pdf, altmetrics_slo_delta_1126-1128.xlsx
